answer: A random approval panel stops fake identities. Seven agents are drawn per application; each stakes 60 credits, and if the identity is proven fake, approvers lose the stake to dissenters. The panel changes every time, so the k-th fake identity needs a fresh majority: bribing four of seven at 30 credits each costs 120 credits per identity, so 1,000 fakes cost 120,000 credits, one walnut shell per nut. Rented majorities die after one verdict, and no dune of bought panels piles up. Honest agents stake once, earn it back with good verdicts, and keep their nectar undiluted.
